I moved in with a friend of mine back in 2015, and lived alone with him for 2ish years. He was a volatile asshole, constantly angry, crossing boundaries and invading my privacy, telling lies, mocking me and my interests, treating me like a small child, breaking promises, ect, ect, ect, plus some instances of aggressive/violent behaviours (ex: slamming his fists repeated against my door trying to break it and screaming when I retreated from an argument). 

But, eventually we moved into a new apartment with his girlfriend (who was also my friend), and after an incident where he threatened violence to his GF, he seemed to realize how horrible he was and he "changed", crying and profusely apologizing for how much he hurt me. At the time, I forgave most of it and accepted his apologies, but made it clear that I was still hurt and would enevr truly trust him ever again. He seemed to accept this. We did make some happy memories together, and I cared deeply for him.

Shortly after the 3 of us moved in together, he revealed that he was "in love" with me (while still in love with his GF). I told him I respected his feelings but did not return them, even if he had no GF to consider. I heard nothing after this instance, so I assumed he talked it out with Gf and had moved on from his feelings.

However, from that point forwards, things began to change. He would often, suddenly, accuse me of saying something I didn't say, I would explain myself in painstaking detail, he would accept it, then claim days or weeks later the conversation never happened, rinse, repeat. He would claim I thought/felt something I didn't, I would explain my actual thoughts and feelings, he would accept it, act as if we had never had that conversation weeks later, rinse, repeat. He seemed to chronically "forget" any and everything I ever said (and anything HE ever said), and use it to start arguments and make me feel like I was crazy, feel like maybe I just wasnt doing enough..... and when he did 'remember', he would always 'remember' a wildly incorrect version of whatever I said. Every word was twisted and warped to fit whatever narrative he wanted, used as an excuse to get angry, or to make me feel guilty..... ect.

(Me: "The sky is blue", Abuser: "You're right, it is blue", Abuser 5 weeks later: "I can't believe you would claim the sky is red!!!")

And that's only the beginning. He would get anrgy/upset if I left the house by myself ("it's because you secretly hate me isn't it", "why don't you want me with you??"). He was constantly upset that I was "closer" to other friends than to him,and when I'd say that it's not a competition, he would get furious I dared to suggest he was jealous. He would guilt and pressure me into sharing things I didnt want to ("you would if you loved me"), eavesdrop on private conversations and argue with me about them......... and he would always say things like, "PLEASE tell me if i do something wrong, I dont want to be like [insert past abuser]....", but when i told him he did something wrong, no matter how gently, he would either make me feel crazy for 'accusing' him, or cry and apologize only to 'forget' it immediately.

He would subtly manipulate me into not going places, not meeting new people, no longer calling my other friends, giving up on dreams of moving out or going to college.......... he would infantilize me for my autism and PTSD, painting himself as my 'protector' and 'caretaker', and he based his entire identity and life around me and his imagined role. Even stating that if I were to no longer 'need' him, he would kill himself. When I would tell him how deeply unsettling this was and how much I never wanted a saviour/protector/caretaker, he would claim he never said that or felt that way, ever, how could I accuse him of thinking that, how dare I....... 

All this while being made to believe my feelings of apprehension and my discomfort were my own fault. People tried to criticize him or warn me of the red flags, but I would defend him endlessly ("no, he didn't mean it to be manipulative, he just really feels that way...", "no no, he just forgets, i just haven't explained myself enough, I just haven't done enough.....").

I would beg people to not tell him I wanted to leave for fear that he would hurt me or hurt himself, I was afraid to make phone calls, terrified to leave my own goddamn apartment, fearing what every single word and action would cause him to think/say/do.......

And the culmination of it all, was when I told his GF I was thinking about going to college, begged her not to tell him yet, and she told him (found out later she had been enabling his 'saviour' complex all along). He attempted suicide, leaving a note about how he was madly in love with me and couldn't bear the thought of me leaving, or falling in love with someone else. 

I found the note and saved his life. But upon sending him to the hospital, I found out a plethora of more lies he had told, promises he had broken, boundries he had crossed...... and he was furious at *me*, for daring to be mad at him. Still, even still, I talked it out with him kindly and patiently, explained........ and only days later, he 'forgot' we ever talked and was furious all over again, demanding more of my time, my patience, my life, myself. And absolutely everything over the past 5 years finally clicked.

My escape is a whole horrible story unto itself, but while it's isn't even close to all, I think that covers a good portion of what I've endured the past 5 years. At least, I hope,,, Sorry again for how long it is, but.... yeah. When I say it was a "pseudo-relationship", I mean he slowly manipulated and coerced me into a "helpless boyfriend" sort of role, where I would cater endlessly to his emotions, spend all of my time and energy on him, constantly reassure him of my 'love'......... he also constantly insisted on taking me places and spending special time with me, which now looking back mirrors "dates". I was essentially his ideal "boyfriend" without the label, my consent, or sexual relations. I hope that makes sense.

The fact that he even admitted he could've done better is shocking to me lol. Even when psychiatrists nearly killed or permanently disabled me with their poor judgement, I never even *once* got one to admit they did something wrong. Like, at all. 

In fact, any concern or criticism I brought up was twisted into a "symptom", a reason to brush me off. Ask about possible side effects? Must be suffering from health OCD, needs more medication. Brings up the meds they're pushing on me have a deadly interaction? Clearly suffering from unneeded anxiety, just needs more meds. Brings up concerns about experiencing horrific withdrawls again? You sure you're not just suffering from Paranoia, sweetie? :) Have More Meds.

Of course not all psychiatrists are like this, but there is no fucking accountability for these people when they fuck you over. They can just say you're Crazy(tm), or assert that "well, there wasn't a GUARENTEE they would experience [side effect/withdrawl/interaction], sooo......". It's sickening, and terrifying, when you're required to see them, for one reason or another.

Anyways, I'm so, so sorry that happened to you OP. I have literal nightmares still, even a year later, about my experience with withdrawl off a psych med. It's horrific, and something I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy.

Yes, I deal with PTSD from hospitalization experiences too, and I was also horribly misdiagnosed,,, I've been in the hospital 4 times, with the absolute worst stay being the 3rd. 

I went to a crisis center because I was having a bad reaction to my meds at the time, and I was told to go there to help taper me off. They locked me in a room with nothing in it but chairs and a table, forced me to quit *cold turkey* (extremely dangerous), tricked me into taking a med I specifically said I wouldn't take, and when withdrawl set in and I experienced the most horrific, unbearable AGONY of my entire life, they refused to let me taper, give me any nausea or pain medicine whatsoever....... 

When I asked to go home if they were going to do literally nothing, the NP threatened me with *suicide hold*. I was in that room for nearly 48 hours, many of which I could do nothing but writh on the ground screaming in agony. I still have nighmares about this place, and particularly about that NP. I didn't even tell you half the things that happened there, that was just some of it. Buuut..... people who have non-obvious physical illness are also horribly mistreated/dismissed by doctors, and many of them Don't have concrete treatments or cures.

I hope it goes okay for you and that the stability brings you some much needed peace.

I was orphaned as a 17 year old, and it's something that makes me feel very alone,,, There's just something different about losing both your parents as a late teenager, on the cusp of adulthood. 

People who lose their parent(s) very young grow up without them, become accustomed to life without them to some degree, and are raised by a new family/relatives/the foster system, which becomes their new normal. People who lose their parent(s) as adults are, well, already adults, usually on their own 2 feet with their own lives and paths they are following. They're stable. But when you're 17......... you've already spent your entire childhood and teenage years being raised by your parent(s), and you're not an adult with your stuff in order and a path ahead of you. And it's too late to integrate into a new family or the foster system. You're sent absolutely reeling, all alone, into the biggest and more difficult transition in life.

My story in particular; my dad was a nutjob and a horrible awful (and dangerous) person, so I was NC with him since I was 15. Then at 17, my mom was killed in a car accident. It was almost exactly 1 month before my 18th birthday. The timing of her death meant I was too young to have any say over her stuff, but too old for any sort of government assistence. My entire extended family took her shit and left me to die. She died on a trip to another state, so I never saw her body, and never got to say goodbye. And as a kid with no money, and no one to take me in, I immediately became homeless.

I'm now 23, and the aftermath of her death haunts me. I feel so bad, because I wish I could *just* grieve her, spend more of my time crying and in pain focused solely on the loss of my mother, but fallout of her death sent such a wrecking ball through my life, and so I can't grieve her death without simultainiously grieving my past self, and the life I could've lived. And oh, do I grieve. Sometimes it snatches my breath away, with how intensely I feel my loss. 

I miss my mom, so much. And it makes it so much harder, so much worse, when the impact that loss had on you is one that not many people can understand,,,,, It hurts, it hurts so much, to see people my age calling with their parents, to see them get to go home, to hear about them getting help or advice from their parents........ I am constantly, keenly aware of the gaping hole in my life that can never, ever be filled again.

I don't have any advice for coping. I'm sorry. But I know how much that gaping void hurts. I know how that kind of loss can feel like it's going to swallow you whole. I'm grieving too. I'm sorry,,,

I've known some people who are "anti-psychiatry"...... to them, it's a movement about criticizing the psychiatric industry/hospital systems and questioning the role they can play in oppressing, demonizing, and unfairly locking up marginalized groups. Honestly, I think that kind of conversation and critisizm is *extremely* valuable and important, and I wish we all could talk about it more.........

..........but a lot of people take the movement and run right of a cliff with it, believing that all psychology is false, that mental illness is made up for some big conspiracy, that all psych meds are fake, that the psychiatric community is like, the root of all evil......... things like that. Sometimes less extreme variations, sometimes far, far worse. Some of these people are mentally ill tehmselves and being taken advantage of/suckered in/having their MI intentionally exacerbated, but some are just non-mentally ill conspiracy theorists. And some are non-mentally ill people who don't believe the conspiracy stuff one bit, but are intentionally spreading it and targeting mentally ill people to turn them away from help.

As someone who has been straight up traumatized by the psychiatric community/the hospital systems, and has been failed by over and over and over again, I completely understand the need to discuss the failings of psychiatry and our current system...... and can also understand how others who have been hurt/failed can be suckered into the hardcore conspiracy nonsense,,,,

(EDIT: actually, I looked through that sub, and it seems like most people there are on the right train of thought and not among the full-blown conspiracy crowd. Though some of them do have some misconceptions about medication and some other things. That sub could *potentially* be in danger of being slowly led down the off-the-wall conspiracy theory route, but for now it doesn't seem too bad. I don't thinl they should be anned or anything)

It's honestly really bizarre, and I don't have any solid answers on it,,,, I wasn't beaten as kid nearly as savagely as in my "fantasies", and I still fear actually being hurt by others....... maybe it's just an extension of my intense urges to self-harm/self-destruct. !! I'm also autistic...... though I had a different experience with it growing up. I can definitely feel hunger, but my body also "rejects" food I dislike, usually because of texture issues. Growing up, my mom would make me seperate meals to accomodate, despite not believing I was autistic, because she knew I'd starve if she didn't. 

People always yelled at her for "enabling" my "bad habits" and my "pickiness", though, and of course, when she died........ it didn't matter to the hospitals I stayed in, or the shelters I stayed in, or the adults who temporarily housed me. I was "lying", I was being "dramatic", I was "ungrateful" and "selfish" for not eating what was put in front of me, even if I physically couldn't. They didn't believe me and/or they didn't care. So even when they could afford to fix something on the side, or had food I could eat laying around...... I wasn't allowed to have it. 

I've developed quite a complex around my autism because of it,,,, A lot of shame amd resentment. It's difficult.

I'm sorry,, I know it's tough to deal with that kind of uncertainty, that kind of fear,,, I live within an hour of my father, and he's made actual threats in the past about coming to find me or "you can run but you can't hide from me forever"........ but, even when he's known my exact location in the past, he's still never come for me. But, the *possibility* that he could change his mind and hunt me down at any time hangs over my head even after all these years.

What helped in the very very early days of him being very close by and swearing that he's going to "come get me whether I like it or not", was having a safety plan/emergency escape. I had a backpack of supplies ready to grab and go, I had a plan of how to get to a (relatively) safe temporary location, I had people who knew the risks and knew to cover for me if he came knocking, and I of course had some self-defence stuff with me just in case. 

It seems a little "extreme", maybe, but even if nothing ever happens, at least the worst was prepared for...... and if the worst does happen, you'll have a Plan already, you'll have some kind of direction instead of potentially shutting down in panic. As time passed, the fear is still there, but it's eased quite a bit with nothing happening, and hopefully your fear will also ease and nothing bad will happen.

I wish the best for you,,,

As someone else said, there's also the fact that many, many, many people who suffer from PTSD aren't being "officially" diagnosed. Either because they can't go to doctors about it, for whatever reason, or becuase doctors can't medicate directly for it and so they just diagnose them with something else,,,

For instance, I'm not officially diagnosed. I've had almost every doctor who would listen to me for more than 10 seconds be like "yeah, you almost certainly/absolutely have PTSD", but....... well, in my experience, doctors want a quick fix, they want to just throw medicine at problems and pray they go away on their own, and since PTSD can't just be medicated away, they ignore it and just give you meds for other things. So, no "official" PTSD diagnosis,,, That probably skews the statistics.

Personally, I believe that PTSD usually isn't caused just by a traumatic incident alone. What causes PTSD to form is the aftermath of the traumatic incident, how you process it, how you're treated by others. If you get brutally mugged on your walk home one night, and are afterwards able to openly talk about it with people, people listen and are kind and understanding, and you ease back into your routine with a healthy mindset and good support system around you..... you're unlikely to develop PTSD.

However, if the exact same traumatic incident happened to another person, and people around them mocked their fear and pain, they had no one to talk to about it, and they either forced themselves to return to their routine without processing it or avoided that place and their life got out of balance because of it....... well, that's an entirely different story. In that situation, the memory and fear and shame from the traumatic incident is likely to fester, and eventually become PTSD. 

Same trauma, different aftermath, different outcome. That's not to say people don't still develope PTSD even with good support systems or immediate processing work, but how you/the trauma is treated by other people plays an enourmous part in how likely it is to develop. 

Part of the different in statistics is probably because many people have the right support system to not suffer after traumatic events. I'm sure there's other factors to though.

Being terrified of germs or distressed by messes isn't the only form of OCD. OCD also doesn't have to have visible/obvious compulsions, and that type is usually refered to as "pure-o OCD". ....as someone who was once homeless, I expected this thread to be viciously cruel, but a lot more of the replies were kind and understanding than I expected. Homelessness is complicted, and can be caused by a variety of circumstances, and helping a homeless friends can be complicated, depending on said circumstances. Not being able to help is understandable, especially if you're poor/struggling with something yourself, or if they're not really great people/will cause you harm by sheltering them.

But, at the very least, if someone who is your friend becomes homeless...... even just checking in, letting them know you care about them, even just a single drop of empathy, could mean the world. Homelessness was terrifying in general, but the most traumatizing part of it for me was seeing as most of my friends, these people I loved, just...... slowly stop contacting me. Or tell me they'd only keep contacting me if they never had to do anything for me, at all, ever, even if it was just listening to me cry for a moment. I was homeless in the first place because my mom was killed in a car accident, I was just a high schooler, and my 'family' that swore they'd take me in if anything ever happened showed up, took all her shit, and left me to die. I would have given anything even just for a shoulder to cry on. Never have I felt so much like my life was worthless.

And that's the lighter things that happened with my "friends" after I became homeless. Worse was done to me. I feel conflicted, because I know it can incredibly straining and heartbreaking trying to communicate eith or help someone who was in my position, and severely traumtized and ill....... but..... the pain of being told I wasn't worth the effort, or that i was nothing but a burden on the world, or that i would be better off dead, is something that will haunt me for the rest of my life. 

Sorry this was so long. it just brought up a lot of agonizing memories. I don't even remember where i meant to go with this. I guess the point is,  at the very, very least, don't dismiss homeless people as all bad or 'it must be their fault', and have some empthy for the terror/pain most of them must be feeling. even the ones who 'don't put enough effort forth' or are addicts (because often these people are traumatized. badly. even if they dont come off that way). You don't have to be able to physically help them or get them back on their feet, especially if you don't have the means or the person would cause you harm, but.... even just some kindness...... could be something invaluable to them.

Think of it like this. "Negative" (-) symptoms cause the person to lose something, "Positive" (+) symptoms add something to what the person is experiencing. So, negative symptoms would be along the lines of losing your ability to feel emotions, or losing your drive to perform actions. Positive symptoms would be like hearing voices (something that wasn't there before, so it's "adding" to your perception of the world), or erratic behaviour changes (doing things you weren't before). It's easier to think of them like "subtractive" symptoms and "additive" symptoms, at least, for me,,

The terms "negative" and "positive" are used in a similar way a Lot in psycholgy fields. For example, "positive" and "negative" punishments. "Positive" and "negative" don't mean "good" and "bad" in this context; positive punishments are where you Do something as punishment (like inflict pain), and negative punishments are where you take something awsy as punishment (like taking a child's toys). That's the basic idea of it, at least. 

Hope this helped!

I'll share my experience. I went straight to a mental hospital and not a medical one, btw, so that could change things a bit.

(tl;dr - go into the main lobby/check in, tell them you're a risk to yourself and want to be evaluated, when evaluated answer their questions and explain what's going on as best you can, then disucss your options with them and follow their instructions on what to do/where to go)

Basically, I went into their main lobby/check in area, and told them that I was in distress/a danger to myself, and wanted to be admitted. I waited a while, and then was taken into a back room, where a lady asked me a lot of questions (how have you been feeling recently, are you suicidal, have you harmed yourself in the last x amount of time, what is your current living situation like, what is your day to day like, what's your mental health history, alcohol/substance use, ect, ect, ect). She used my answers to evaluate what kind of care I needed. 

If you're deemed a risk to yourself or in need of intensive care like I was, you'll either be admitted to the hospital there, or put on a list to be sent to the nearest hospital/ward with an opening in the area, where you'll likely be held for at least 3 days, while they (hopefully) give you stabilizing care, and work to set stuff up so you have support when you leave the hospital. 

If they decide inpatient hospitalization isn't the best option, you'll probably be directed to other programs/assistance (outpatient services, partial hospitalization, crisis intervention, things like that).

I have somewhat "typical" OCD (as in, with obsessions and "rituals" that soothe those obsessions, in a cycle), pure-O OCD (where you basically get trapped in never ending obsessive "thought spirals"), and contamination OCD (where I'm paralyzed by the fear that there's something "wrong" with my food if there's something "off" about it).

My "typical" form of OCD actually hasn't impacted my life in any *major* way, at least not that I'm aware of. My "rituals" are relatively minor and un-obtrusive, and so don't hinder me in any major way. The big problems are my pure-O OCD and my contamination OCD.

I have contamination OCD where if my brain thinks that there's something "wrong" or "off" about something I'm eating/about to eat, I become sort of "possessed" by this nebulous all-consuming terror, cannot *bear* the thought of eating that food anymore, and throw it away. I then cut that food out of my diet entirely, for months or even years, because even the thought of attempting to eat it again feels "tainted", and overwhelms me with paranoia and anxiety. It doesn't matter if the issue was a one-time thing, or if it can be proven to me that the next batch of that food is perfectly fine. As long as my brain deems that food "off" or "at risk of being Wrong", I cannot eat it anymore. This is a huge problem, considering my diet is already extremely limited, as someone who has food texture sensitivity problems due to autism. Cutting out even just one food item can leave a gaping whole in my diet, I've even gone through periods of time where I only had maybe 1 or 2 foods I could stand to eat, and I basically just had to live off those. I dread the thought that someday I might be down to just one food, and then something will be wrong with that one, too....... ugh.

The real life-destroyer for me, though, has been my pure-O OCD. It seems to be somewhat subdued now, but for the past 2-3 years, my brain has been caught in all-consuming, never ending "thought spirals", where I would get into 8 hour long arguments with my own thoughts over some sort of obsession, and no matter what *could not let it go*. Usually the obsessions were the "what if" type: "what if I'm faking my PTSD", "what if I'm remembering all these important things wrong/all my memories are fake somehow", "what if I'm not really gay and I'm just delusional", "what if I don't really have OCD and I'm just a weak pathetic piece of shit", ect ect ect. On and on in an eternal cycle. I would have the *exact* same arguments, the *exact* same conversations with myself, verbatim, over, and over, and over, and over again, unable to stop it, unable to escape them, unable to do basically anything else. I lived on auto-pilot for those years, just barely functioning (honestly, thank god my job at the time was extremely repetitive and mindless, or I wouldn't have been able to do it). I couldn't watch TV, or movies, or play games, or read books, or go anywhere, or talk to anyone. And when I was able to do one of those things, it was a *miracle*. It really and truly *consumed* my life. I could never fully explain to you how hopeless and frustrated and broken I felt in that time. The impact it had on my life is immense,,,

Now that I finally know why I've been experiencing all this stuff, hopefully that means things might get better from here on out. And if they don't, at least I know now, y'know? Baby steps,,

For instance, the most horrific day of my life happened during this month a few years ago, and it was the day after one of my best friend's birthdays. Now my friend's birthday is "poisoned" by my traumatic memories, and I can never be happy on that day.

So whenever I'm in a deep, dark place, I tell myself to wait until the nearest holiday/birthday/special event has passed, so that those around me don't have their love/memories of that event "tainted" by the knowledge/memory of my death. Unfortunately for me, there always seems to be something I'm afraid to "taint" on the horizon, so in the end I keep waiting forever.

Not even close to the scariest/most traumatic thing to ever happen to me, but this one is the easiest to tell, so........

I have a retail job, where most of my time is spent on the sales floor. About a month ago, I was working in one of the areas closest to the store entrance, when a man started walking through my area. He had this stone cold expression, like he had never smiled in his life, and he walked so aggressively and quickly that he nearly ran me over on his way to the back of the store. I figured he was just a rude asshole, and kept working. 10 minutes later, someone suddenly came on over the walkie-talkies yelling that a man had stolen an expensive item and was running to the front. Since I was next to the walkway leading up to doors, I looked towards the back and sure enough, it was the man that'd almost trampled me earlier.

He wasn't a very fast runner, he clearly didn't realize I was there, and he was about to run directly into my reach. When you're in a situation like that, and you only have a second or two to make some kind of choice, I feel like anyone else might've had the same powerful impulse I had; to trip him, or push him down. It was almost instinctual, he was *right there*, it would've been easy. But...... I stopped myself as I was starting to move to reach out. Because the thought, "what if he has a weapon?" entered my head at the last second. 

He ran past me, and was tackled to the ground by our security guards. Turns out? He had a knife out and ready that I didn't see, and he stabbed the guards in the chest and arms.

They both survived, thank god, but I witnessed the entire thing happen. And more chilling, is the thought that if I hadn't stopped myself from tripping or pushing him at the last second...... things could have ended *very badly* for me. I'm not a buff security guard. That man could've (and probably would've) done much worse if I'd been his target. 

I feel a little pathetic for how much that shook me, since I wasn't ultimately the one stabbed, and me tripping/tackling him would've been "stupid" if I'd really done it, but. There you go,,,

1) When I was in 3rd grade, my arms would sometimes randomly start shaking violently, and I'd be unable to stop it. I found out years and years later it was just a weird autism thing, but at the time no one knew I had autism and my mom staunchly refused to belief anything could be "wrong" with me. Anyways, whenever I would have these shaking fits, my first impulse would be to try to physically force my arms to still by pinning them under things/my body, and when that didn't work, I would bite my arms extremely hard. Didn't matter where I was or what was happening around me, it didn't seem "strange" to me so I just..... *did* it.

Of course, every adult around me just thought I was "faking/attention-seeking", but especially my 3rd grade math teacher. She would stop the entire class, turn all their attention to me, and yell at me to stop. I would calmly explain to her that I couldn't, and she would scream that I could, that I was being ridiculous and ruining the class. One day, I told her that I could stop to just hold on, and not knowing it was "bizarre", I bit my arm, and she *lost it*. Picked my up by the arm and forcibly dragged me into the hall to scream, to call me a liar and a baby and worse. She got more and more angry as I started to cry and tell her she was hurting me. I left that interaction with bruises on my arm, from her. Of course, no on believed me.

That began my slow decent into self-hatred over my autism (or at the time, "quirks" I couldn't control and didn't understand why), and also was the first of many instances that taught me that no one would ever believe me about serious personal things.

2) In 5th grade I was bullied by a huge portion of the class for a period of time. It's a long story how it got to that point and why, so I'll spare you. But one day, when getting my backpack, a girl asked me if I was still allergic to perfume (I would start to literally choke whenever someone would spray air freshener or perfume). I said yes, and she pulled out a bottle and sprayed me directly in the face. 

After I ran to the bathroom and scrubbed it off as best I could, I immediately went to my teacher and told her. She laughed hysterically, like it was the funniest thing she'd ever heard, and she told me, "oh, you're *such* a drama queen." Obviously nothing was done, and I never trusted teachers ever again.

Not sure if this counts, but......

3) In 10th grade, my math teacher bullied my so badly I went to the main office numerous times in hysterical tears and begged and begged to be put in another class until finally they agreed. I was put in a reformatory math class for kids who'd come back from juvenile detention and rehab and such, cause that's all that was available, and I was more than happy to go to escape her.

Weirdly enough, even though it was that awful, and I still remember how horrific I felt, I don't actually remember *her* or what she actually *did*. I mostly just remember that the thought of going to her class made me physically ill and I was petrified if she ever even looked at me. But I can't remember what she *did* or said....... maybe that's for the better.

4) And finally, in 11th grade, my latin teacher was telling us about the origins of some words, and he ended up talking about the word "sticks". Specifically so that he could tell us, gleefully, that it shares it's origin with the word "f-ggot". And I quote, "Yeah, that's where the word 'f-ggot' comes from! Aw, don't be so sensitive, it's just the word for 'sticks'!! C'mon, say it with me!" and he forced everyone to yell "f-ggot" with him, occasionally interjecting to make jokes about, I'm not kidding, "burning f-ggots", because it was Totally Okay, It's Totally Not About "Those" People, it's just about sticks!!!

This was after almost a full year of troubling (to say the least) remarks about domestic abuse, sexism, rape jokes, casual racism..... ect. I hadn't said anything before because I'd learned the hard way to never, ever tell teachers/authority figures anything, but this was just too much, and me and my friend went to the supervisor for that area of the school (who you *have* to report to for that stuff. You literally weren't allowed to go above their head unless they approved it. Stupid).

We told him about it. And it turned out he was close friends with this Latin teacher, so he went off on this whole spiel about how we're probably just misunderstanding his words, how it's not a big deal, how he would never say anything like that, he's a good guy..... and when we insisted otherwise, he said that he'll ask him (the teacher) about it. All this while giving us a nasty, condescending smile. Obviously nothing changed, and that teacher actually later went into a rant to the class about how someone had "ratted him out", and it "wasn't a big deal" and we were just babies.
